about: Proposed unit, category, land kind and need of each existing resource (D1, D3). Proposals, to be confirmed; catalogue.py joins them to the facts from the XML. Roles (D16): every system the statement names in which a good takes part, with the existing buildings and units it touches; "need" is the need role only, kept for catalogue.py.

role_kinds.need: consumed per citizen to meet a need (statement 3.3); effects of supply and of shortfall; component CN
role_kinds.material: used up to make something: buildings, units, tools, other goods (3.2, 3.5); components PR.F3, IN.F1, IN.F2
role_kinds.fuel: burnt for heat in homes and in workshops (3.3 fuel need; 3.5 recipes); components CN, IN.F1
role_kinds.storage: how the good keeps: perishable or durable, and what preserves it (3.1, 3.4); components SD.F1, SD.F2, FG.F2

production.about: Proposal for PR.F1 (R10, M53): a worked tile's output from the real people employed on it, the technologies and resources available, land quality and the kind of good. Status: open (D23). Figures marked 'source' come from the sources listed; figures marked 'estimate' are mine, to be replaced by sourced ones.

model.formula: output per year (tonnes) = area worked (ha) x gross yield (t/ha) x land quality x (1 - seed share)
model.area_worked: min(the tile's farmland, workers x hectares per worker); the tile's farmland is open (D23 question 3)
model.workers: decided (M54): the game's real population per working citizen (size^2.8 x 1000 / size) times the share of people who work (estimate 40 %, to be sourced): about 400 at size 1, 17,000 at size 8, 88,000 at size 20
model.yield: per good and technology stage; the game's own farm techs (IMPROVEMENT_FARM TechYieldChanges) are the stages
model.land_quality: a multiplier per tile and good: today from terrain, fresh water and the placed resource; land qualities (LD) replace it later
model.time: decided (M54): flows per year while a turn lasts a year or more; a turn shorter than a year (at Normal speed 6 months for 150 turns, then 3 months for 20) produces and consumes its fraction of a year
model.integers: whole tonnes per year; a size-20 city of 4.4 million at about 0.25 t of grain each eats about 1.1 million t a year, far below 2^31 (rule F)

game_facts.real_population: CvCity::getRealPopulation = size^2.8 x 1000: size 1 = 1,000; size 8 = 337,000; size 20 = 4.4 million (per citizen: 1,000; 42,000; 220,000)
game_facts.turn_length_normal: GAMESPEED_NORMAL (CIV4GameSpeedInfo.xml): 50 years a turn for 40 turns, 25 for 100, 20 for 120, 10 for 50, 5 for 80, 2 for 80, 1 for 60, half a year for 150, a quarter for 20: 700 turns
game_facts.farm_techs: IMPROVEMENT_FARM: +2 food irrigated; +1 food each at Fermentation, Mathematics, Waterworks, Crop Rotation, Biology, Pesticides, Machine Tools (-1 production), Gene Manipulation

stages.basis: source: Winchester manors c.1300 gross 0.515 t/ha, net 0.385, 4 grains per grain sown (Pretty 1990); Columella 42 person-days/ha before harvest (White 1965), 78 with missing tasks (Rosenstein): 250 working days give 3-6 ha
estimate: Roman estate management; Kent manors before 1303 about 0.8 t/ha at 2.9 grains per grain (Mate 1985, my conversion)
estimate: four-course rotation with clover; to be sourced (English yields about 1800)
source: UK wheat just over 2 t/ha in the early 20th century (Mackay et al. 2020, PMC7211843); US wheat 56 worker-hours per acre in 1800
estimate for yield; source for labour: US wheat 3 worker-hours per acre by 1970 (about 7 h/ha)
source: UK wheat about 8 t/ha today (Mackay et al. 2020)

wheat.not_mapped: Waterworks: irrigation, raises land quality on watered land (proposed). Fermentation: see fermentation below (corrected after M54).
wheat.example: Before Mathematics, 17,000 workers on a good wheat tile (a size-8 city's citizen: 42,000 people x 40 %): 17,000 x 3 ha x 0.5 t x 1.0 x 0.75 = 19,125 t a year, if the tile's farmland is at least 51,000 ha; the city's 337,000 people at about 0.2 t of grain each eat about 67,000 t

land_quality_today.basis: estimate; rich = flood plains or a river with the crop's resource, good = grassland or plains with the resource or fresh water, poor = otherwise; the best single Winchester harvest (1.8 t/ha against 0.5) shows the spread is real

production.other_goods: The same model per good: rice (higher yield, more labour per ha), corn, potato (fresh weight), livestock (head and product per head per year: milk, wool, hides), timber (cubic metres or tonnes per woodcutter per year), ore (tonnes per miner per year). Written after D23 is decided, each with sources.
sources: Pretty, J. (1990) Sustainable Agriculture in the Middle Ages: The English Manor, Agricultural History Review 38: https://www.bahs.org.uk/AGHR/ARTICLES/38n1a1.pdf
Mate, M. (1985) Medieval Agrarian Practices: The Determining Factors?, Agricultural History Review 33: https://www.bahs.org.uk/AGHR/ARTICLES/33n1a2.pdf
Columella, De Re Rustica II.12 (via secondary summaries; White 1965, Spurr, Rosenstein): https://acoup.blog/2025/09/05/collections-life-work-death-and-the-peasant-part-ivb-working-days/
Mackay, I. et al. (2020) estimating the upper yield boundary of winter wheat: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7211843/
US worker-hours per acre of wheat 1800-1970 (teaching resource): https://www.digitalhistory.uh.edu/disp_textbook.cfm?psid=3837&smtID=11
Sourdough Bread Quality: Facts and Factors (review): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11241011/
Effects of sourdough or regular bread fermentation and phytate reduction on iron (systematic review, 2026): https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2026.1778997/full
Leenhardt et al., moderate decrease of pH by sourdough fermentation reduces phytate: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8098531

fermentation.correction: My first proposal said Fermentation leaves wheat unchanged. Wrong (M54): fermentation does not change the tonnes harvested, but it changes how much of the grain's nutrition people get from each tonne eaten, and how the grain keeps (bread, sourdough, beer, malted and fermented porridges).
facts: Sourdough fermentation degrades phytic acid by up to 96.6 % with mixed fermentation, against up to 56 % with yeast alone; a slight acidification to pH 5.5 cuts phytate by about 35 % (review, PMC11241011; Leenhardt et al.)
Bioavailability of iron and zinc in bread rises by about 10 % and 25 % with sourdough fermentation, from a low base (about 10 % for iron, 25 % for zinc from wheat) (review, PMC11241011)
Whole-wheat sourdough fermented 4 hours at 30 C: iron and zinc absorption up over 30 % in vivo, with 60 % less phytate (cited in the same review)
Sorghum fermented with Rhizopus, Lactobacillus plantarum and yeast: protein digestibility 3.5 to 5 times the unfermented control, protein content unchanged (Agritech 2017)
Malted sorghum and millet: protein digestibility 34.5-68.1 %; fermented flours 97.4-98.3 % (study in the same search)
Against too large an effect: a 2026 systematic review finds higher iron bioavailability in acute trials but no better iron status in long-term trials (Frontiers in Nutrition, fnut.2026.1778997)
fermentation.proposal: Each food good gets a food value per tonne (the nutrition people get from it; FG and CN use it). Fermentation raises the food value of the cereals people ferment (wheat, barley in beer, rice, corn, sorghum and millet where present) and lets them keep longer as bread and drink (SD.F2). Size: estimate +15 % food value for cereals, between the mineral gains (+10 % iron, +25 % zinc) and the protein gains for coarse grains, kept modest because long-term human trials show smaller effects. The game's own +1 farm food at Fermentation matches this reading: food value, not harvest.
fermentation.where: FG.F1 (food value of staple goods), CN.F1 (needs met per tonne), SD.F2 (keeping)

farmland.status: decided (M55): option (i), a scale declared per map or scenario; compatibility by editing the mod's scenarios and map scripts automatically (PR.F6)
facts: CIV4WorldInfo.xml has no scale field (its tags: grid width and height, maintenance, research and other modifiers); the world sizes run from Duel (40 x 24 plots) to Gigantic (200 x 120 plots), and the same Earth-like map can be played at any of them
A city works at most NUM_CITY_PLOTS = 21 plots (CvDefines.h, radius 2)
Real population grows as size^2.8 x 1000, the same on every map and world size
The mod has 44 WorldBuilder scenarios and 39 map scripts, all in PrivateMaps (GitLab ba209b49)

Scenarios are read by the base game's pyWB/CvWBDesc.py, which the mod does not ship (codemap/python.md lists it from the base game); the mod's own EntryPoints/CvWBInterface.py calls WBDesc.read, applyMap and write

Map scripts are Python modules the DLL calls by function name through gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction (CvMapGenerator.cpp: addRivers, addFeatures, addBonuses, ...); a missing function falls back to the default

Of the 44 scenarios, 8 cover the whole Earth (wrap X, latitude 90 to -90: Earth 3/12/18/23/28 preset civs, Earth Ice Age, Giant Earth Map x3, RFC Earth), 3 CarterEarth to -66, many regional maps carry latitude 0..0 (unset), Mars two maps, and fictional maps (Tamriel x2, Orion, Sirius)

The whole-Earth scenarios show 36-38 % of their plots as land against Earth's 29 % (148.9 of 510.1 million km2): land is drawn larger than the sea, so the scale from Earth's whole surface over all plots and the scale from Earth's land over the land plots differ by about 27 % (Earth Standard 84 x 52: 116,780 against 91,630 km2 per plot)
'Democragphica, Huge Mediterranean' and 'Europe' have the same grid, plots and land plots (100 x 73, 4,880 land): to compare plot by plot
options: (i) a scale declared per map or scenario (km^2 per tile), the map's author's choice
(ii) no area: each additional worker on a tile adds less (a diminishing return), with no km^2 at all

(iii) farmland per tile derived from the game's own population numbers, not the map: the area at which a city's land, at the era's yields, feeds the population the game already shows. Example before Mathematics: a size-8 city (337,000 people, 67,000 t of grain a year) at 0.375 t/ha net needs about 180,000 ha of grain land; on about 8 farmed tiles that is about 22,000 ha (220 km^2) of farmland per tile
farmland.note: (iii) ties the scale to what the game already claims about its cities, so the map's size does not enter; it fixes one scale for all maps, which (i) would let a map override

mechanism.scenarios: a block at the end of the file, after every block CvWBDesc reads: 'BeginEconomy / plot area km2=<n> / EndEconomy'; the mod's CvWBInterface.py reads it after WBDesc.read and passes it to the DLL, and appends it again when the WorldBuilder saves; the base game's reader stops before it, so the files still load without the mod
mechanism.map_scripts: an optional function getPlotAreaKm2() in each map script, which the DLL asks for when it generates a map (a whole-planet script can compute it from the grid size: the planet's surface over the number of plots)
mechanism.game: CvMap keeps the value, saved with the map; maps that declare nothing get a default and a log line naming the map
mechanism.values: per map, each with its basis: whole-Earth maps from Earth's surface (510.1 million km2) over the plots; regional maps from the region's real extent; Mars from its surface (144.8 million km2); fictional maps a chosen value, said so; refined later per plot by latitude (cos of latitude) where a map has real latitudes

farmland.facts_per_scenario: research/economy/plan/map_scale_facts.tsv (GitLab a1d9c3f2): grid, plots, land plots (plot types peak, hills, flat), wrap; counted from each scenario's plot records
farmland.method_proposed: the scale for farmland from land: a map's plot area = the real land area of what it shows / its land plots (whole-Earth maps: 148.9 million km2; Mars: 144.8 million km2, all land; regional maps: the land area inside the region the map shows, sourced per map; fictional maps: a chosen value, said so). The whole-surface value is kept beside it as a cross-check

what_each_map_shows.about: Read from renderings of each scenario's land and sea (research/economy/plan/map_scale/sheet1-4.png; green land, tan desert, white snow, ice and tundra), not from the names alone
whole_earth: RFC Earth with big Europe 50 civs (124x68)
CarterEarth x3 (192x120, latitude 90 to -66: no Antarctica)
whole_earth_other: Earth Ice Age (124x68): a whole Earth with more land (45 % of plots)

regional.The Americas with part of Greenland: North and South America (58x72) and Colonization 1500AD (58x72): the same picture
regional.Europe from Iceland and Scandinavia to t: Europe (100x73); Democragphica, Huge Mediterranean renders the same

what_each_map_shows.mars: Mars and Mars Colonization (80x57): Mars with seas (73 % land)

farmland.next_step: Regional values need the real land area inside each map's extent: georeference each map by two landmarks (e.g. Gibraltar and the Bosporus), take its latitude-longitude box, and measure land inside it on a public-domain land mask (Natural Earth); whole-Earth and Mars values from their sourced land areas; fictional maps a chosen value

sectors.about: D26 (M57): proposed sector of each good, for the user to confirm; shown in the second UI mock-up. With no processed goods yet (D3), the artisanal and industrial sectors hold the few made goods the mod has; recipes (IN.F1) fill them later.
